place.source_title: Cargo Warehouse (the old Gilchrist Lumber Company building, c. 1860)

brief: A long two-storey white clapboard warehouse turned shop: a low gable roof, a row of dark awnings over the ground-floor windows, millstones and ironwork displayed along the front walk. Two photos. Older than 1970: Lake Erie island and harbour-town main streets (the Put-in-Bay model) are 19th-century commercial blocks; no newer example of this main-street type exists. Foundations taken deeper than needed (spec rule 4).

facade.notes: the old Gilchrist Lumber warehouse (Vermilion OH, 1860s), now a gift shop ('Cargo'): a big two-storey side-gabled shed in white siding with green awnings and shutters, a loading door, mill stones and pilings as decoration; the town water tower beyond

why.note: a lumber warehouse by the harbour turned into a shop
